summary: RN 0.86.0 Phase 2 verified on Android (New Architecture forced on, real APK builds); iOS Fabric documented not implemented (see docs/new-architecture-ios-followup.md)
detail:
Full migration RN 0.64.2->0.73.11->0.86.0 now complete except iOS native Fabric. What was built: codegenConfig in root package.json (name RNFastImageSpec, type all, jsSrcsDir src); src/FastImageViewNativeComponent.ts (codegenNativeComponent Fabric props spec) and src/NativeFastImageView.ts (TurboModule spec, TurboModuleRegistry.get('FastImageView') - kept the SAME native name for view+module, unlike @d11's fork which splits into 'FastImageView'/'FastImageViewModule'); index.tsx now branches on global.nativeFabricUIManager/global.__turboModuleProxy at runtime to pick Fabric vs old-arch component and TurboModule vs NativeModules, converts source.headers from a map to an array-of-{name,value} under Fabric (Codegen can't type an arbitrary string-keyed map), and only stringifies defaultSource when it's a real number (not under jest's asset-mock object shape). Android got a full oldarch/newarch source-set split (android/src/oldarch, android/src/newarch, mirroring @d11/react-native-fast-image's real published architecture) selected via a newArchEnabled Gradle property check in android/build.gradle; FastImageViewModuleImplementation.java extracts shared preload/clearMemoryCache/clearDiskCache logic; FastImageViewPackage.java converted to TurboReactPackage; new android/.../events/*.java (FastImageLoadEvent etc, Event<T> subclasses) replace raw RCTEventEmitter.receiveEvent calls in FastImageViewWithUrl.java and FastImageRequestListener.java with EventDispatcher/UIManagerHelper (required for Fabric, works fine under old arch too). FastImageViewConverter.getHeaders() now accepts both the old map shape and the new Fabric array shape. iOS Fabric intentionally NOT implemented (no Xcode on this Windows machine) - documented in docs/new-architecture-ios-followup.md with the @d11 fork's actual file layout (FFFastImageViewComponentView.h/.mm, FFFastImageViewModule.h/.mm, codegenConfig.ios.componentProvider) as the reference for whoever picks it up on a Mac.

Real build-breaking issues hit and fixed verifying against actual RN 0.86.0 + New Architecture (beyond the JS/native wiring above): (1) root jest config needed 'preset': '@react-native/jest-preset' - RN 0.86 moved the jest preset out of the react-native package into a separate package. (2) index.tsx had two real bugs caught only by running tests: eagerly capturing NativeModules.FastImageView at import time broke the test's beforeAll-mock pattern (fixed by resolving it lazily inside a getFastImageViewModule() function instead of a top-level const); and `resolvedDefaultSource !== null` let `undefined` slip through and get wrongly stringified (fixed to `typeof resolvedDefaultSource === 'number'`). (3) React 19's react-test-renderer requires renderer.create() to be wrapped in act() now - without it .toJSON() returns null (previously just a console warning, now silently broken) - src/index.test.tsx needed a createTree() helper wrapping every renderer.create() call. (4) Autolinking failed with 'Could not find project.android.packageName in react-native config output' - RN 0.86's settings.gradle uses autolinkLibrariesFromCommand() which shells out to `npx @react-native-community/cli config`; without @react-native-community/cli(+cli-platform-android/-ios) as actual devDependencies, npx silently fetched an incompatible latest-from-registry copy that returned an empty project block. Fixed by adding those three packages back at 20.1.0 (RN 0.86 template's own pinned version) - they'd been dropped when bumping the example app's package.json for this phase. (5) react-native-reanimated 3.19.5 and react-native-screens 3.37.0 (both resolved via caret ranges) used bridge-era APIs removed from RN 0.86 (LayoutAnimationController/UIManagerModuleListener for reanimated, ChoreographerCompat for screens) - same caret-range-outruns-target-RN lesson as Phase 1, except this time the fix was bumping UP to the new-arch-only major (reanimated v3->v4.5.1 + its new react-native-worklets 0.10.0 peer dependency, screens v3->v4.25.2) since New Architecture is now mandatory so the newest majors are actually the correct choice, unlike Phase 1 where newest was wrong. (6) react-native-safe-area-context 4.14.1's Fabric C++ used a removed Yoga API (`facebook::yoga::StyleLength::unit` no longer exists) - bumped to 5.8.0. (7) A genuine Windows-only ninja/CMake infinite loop ('manifest still dirty after 100 tries') hit react-native-reanimated+react-native-worklets' native build - root-caused to Windows Defender real-time protection touching build files mid-compile (confirmed via `ninja -d explain`, which also showed a real second issue: worklets' prefab package genuinely didn't exist yet on first build, a Gradle task-ordering gap). Added a Defender exclusion for the project folder (did not fix it), then built :react-native-worklets:assembleDebug standalone first (did not fix it either - reanimated's own stale .cxx cache still remembered the missing path). Ultimately reanimated/react-native-worklets were removed from the example app entirely (not used anywhere in its JS source, confirmed via grep) rather than sink further time into a third-party library's Windows-CMake bug unrelated to react-native-fast-image itself - this was the user's explicit choice among three offered options. (8) Separately, a genuine Windows MAX_PATH (260 char) limit broke react-native-screens' and react-native-safe-area-context's autolinked Fabric C++ codegen builds (object file paths embedding the full absolute source path ballooned past 260 chars under this repo's deeply nested path) - fixed project-locally (no system/registry change) by adding `externalNativeBuild { cmake { buildStagingDirectory "C:/rncxx" } }` to ReactNativeFastImageExample/android/app/build.gradle, staging CMake/ninja output somewhere short instead of under the deep repo tree.

Final state: `gradlew assembleDebug` BUILD SUCCESSFUL against RN 0.86.0 with newArchEnabled=true, producing a real app-debug.apk with react-native-fast-image's Fabric ViewManager + TurboModule actually compiled and linked. Root `bun run test` also passes 8/8 against React 19.2.3.
why: Every one of these was hit and fixed during actual verification against a real build, not hypothetical - this is exactly the kind of native-toolchain-plus-dependency-version-lag mess a from-scratch New Architecture migration produces, and each fix required figuring out root cause rather than symptom (e.g. the ninja loop needed `ninja -d explain` to find the real reason, not guessing).
how_to_apply: If iOS Fabric work resumes: read docs/new-architecture-ios-followup.md first, do it on a machine with Xcode. If Android native deps need bumping further: same caret-range warning as before, but note the direction flips once New Architecture is mandatory - newest major is usually correct now, not a pinned older release. If Windows CMake builds act up again: check Defender status and `ninja -d explain` output before assuming it's flaky; check for MAX_PATH issues via `externalNativeBuild.cmake.buildStagingDirectory` if paths are deeply nested. reanimated/worklets are NOT currently installed in ReactNativeFastImageExample - if the example app's demo screens ever need animation, that's a deliberate gap to fill back in with a working Windows CMake setup, not an oversight.

how_to_apply: When testing global.nativeFabricUIManager/global.__turboModuleProxy branches in index.tsx, use jest.isolateModules (not a bare jest.resetModules on the shared registry) so the toggle does not leak into other describe blocks. summary: bun run build (root) and bun run test (example app) were never actually run/verified during the Phase 2 migration - both were broken; fixed now
detail:
User ran `bun run test` inside ReactNativeFastImageExample/ (not the root lib) and it failed immediately: jest tried to parse a .png inside node_modules/@react-navigation/elements as JS. Root cause: the example app's package.json jest config still had "preset": "react-native" (the old RN-bundled preset, removed in 0.86 - moved to @react-native/jest-preset, same bug already fixed in root package.json during Phase 2 but never applied here). Fixed: added "@react-native/jest-preset":"0.86.0" devDependency + preset value, and added a "transformIgnorePatterns" override (default preset one does not allow-list @react-navigation, so its packaged .png/.tsx never got transformed) - `"node_modules/(?!(jest-)?react-native|@react-native(-community)?|@react-navigation)/"`.

That then surfaced a second, deeper bug: `Cannot find module 'react-native-fast-image'` because the library's dist/ folder did not exist - `bun run build` had never been run this whole migration (only native gradlew builds were verified, which never touch the JS/Metro path). Running `bun run build` at root then failed on THREE previously-invisible problems, all masked until now because nothing ever actually typechecked/bundled the library:
(1) tsconfig.json had no explicit "types" array, so TS implicit typeRoots scanning pulled in every package under node_modules/@types including a broken stub @types/minimatch@6.0.0 (no actual .d.ts, real minimatch ships its own types now) -> TS2688. Fixed by adding `"types": ["jest", "node", "react", "react-test-renderer"]` to tsconfig.json (node needed for the bare `global` identifier used in index.tsx/index.test.tsx).
(2) src/index.test.tsx's new "forwards ref" test hit TS2769 because FastImage's exported type was `React.ComponentType<FastImageProps> & FastImageStaticProperties`, which does not represent forwardRef/ref-acceptance even though the component genuinely is `forwardRef(...)` under the hood at runtime. This is a REAL pre-existing typing gap only caught because tsc had never actually been run against this file. Fixed by changing the exported type to `React.ForwardRefExoticComponent<FastImageProps & React.RefAttributes<any>> & FastImageStaticProperties` in src/index.tsx - accurate to the actual runtime shape, not a hack.
(3) The biggest one: rollup (dv-scripts build, single-entry `src/index.tsx` -> dist/index.cjs.js + dist/index.js) never bundled `./FastImageViewNativeComponent` or `./NativeFastImageView` because index.tsx called them via conditional `require('./X').default` (runtime CommonJS require inside a ternary) instead of static ES imports - rollup left these as literal `require(...)` calls in the output expecting sibling dist/*.js files that were never emitted (only .d.ts files were, from tsc). Fixed by converting both to static top-level `import FastImageViewComponent from './FastImageViewNativeComponent'` / `import NativeFastImageViewModule from './NativeFastImageView'` in index.tsx, then referencing the already-imported values instead of calling require() inline. This is safe: it does NOT reintroduce the earlier "eager NativeModules.FastImageView capture at import time broke test mocking" bug from Phase 2, because that bug was about the *property lookup* `NativeModules.FastImageView` needing to stay lazy (still is, via getFastImageViewModule()), not about *importing* NativeFastImageView.ts/FastImageViewNativeComponent.ts eagerly - both of those modules resolve safely regardless of architecture (TurboModuleRegistry.get falls back to NativeModules when no turbo proxy; codegenNativeComponent/requireNativeComponent registers the same native view name either way). Fixing (3) surfaced a 4th, purely typing-level issue: `resolvedDefaultSourceAsString` was inferred `string | number | null` but FastImageViewComponent's NativeProps.defaultSource requires `string | null | undefined` (now real HeaderInfo since the import is no longer untyped `any` from a dynamic require) - fixed by explicitly typing that const `any` (matching the existing `resolvedSource: any` convention a few lines above, since the value is genuinely polymorphic across the old-arch numeric-passthrough vs Fabric string-only prop contracts).

Also fixed ReactNativeFastImageExample/__tests__/App-test.tsx (the RN template's own default test, never touched before): `renderer.create(<App />)` was not wrapped in `act()`, so a React 19 async scheduler callback fired after Jest tore down the module registry, throwing "You are trying to import a file after the Jest environment has been torn down" - jest reported the test as PASSING but the process still exited 1 because of the stray post-teardown exception. Same root cause/fix pattern as the root package's createTree() helper, applied here as a one-line act() wrap.

After all of this: `bun run build` succeeds (dist/index.cjs.js now genuinely bundles FastImageViewComponent + NativeFastImageViewModule, verified no leftover `require('./` calls in the output), root `bun run test` still 21/21, and `ReactNativeFastImageExample`'s own `bun run test` (App-test.tsx) passes cleanly with exit code 0.
why: The whole Phase 1/2 migration was previously "verified" only via gradlew assembleDebug (native Android build) - that path never touches Metro/JS bundling or the packaged dist/ output at all, so an entire class of real bugs (stale jest preset, broken dist build, a genuine typing gap, and a template test with the same React-19-act() issue we'd already fixed once) sat undetected. This is the exact gap flagged in the original migration plan's verification checklist ("flag if native builds could not be executed") but for the JS/build side specifically, which had no equivalent flag.
how_to_apply: Do not consider this library "fully verified" from gradlew assembleDebug alone - `bun run build` (root) and `bun run test` (both root AND ReactNativeFastImageExample) must all be run and pass before trusting a change. If index.tsx ever goes back to conditional/dynamic `require()` for architecture branching, re-check that dv-scripts' single-entry rollup config (node_modules/dv-scripts/dist/configs/rollup.js) actually bundles it - it treats relative requires as bundleable only when statically analyzable, not behind a runtime ternary. If tsconfig.json's explicit "types" array (jest/node/react/react-test-renderer) is ever removed, @types/minimatch (or any other broken stub under node_modules/@types) can silently break the build again - keep it explicit.

summary: ReactNativeFastImageExample now genuinely runs on a real Android emulator (screenshot-verified: FastImageView rendering, GIF, border-radius, priority all working under Fabric) after fixing metro.config.js and the run-android workflow on this Windows/Git-Bash setup
detail:
User ran the app for real (previous sessions only ever built gradlew assembleDebug and never launched Metro/JS). Hit a chain of real, previously-invisible bugs:
(1) `Unable to resolve module react-native-fast-image` - metro.config.js was still the bare RN<0.68-style raw object (no getDefaultConfig/mergeConfig at all), and had no watchFolders/symlink support for the bun-linked library living outside this app directory. Rewrote it to `mergeConfig(getDefaultConfig(projectRoot), { watchFolders: [workspaceRoot], resolver: { unstable_enableSymlinks: true, nodeModulesPaths: [...] } })`.
(2) Once that resolved, hit `Unable to resolve module missing-asset-registry-path` for every .png - because the bare custom config (before fix) never had `transformer.assetRegistryPath` wired at all; fixed as part of switching to the proper `mergeConfig(getDefaultConfig(...), ...)` pattern from RN 0.86's real rn-diff-purge template.
(3) Once assets worked, hit real "Invalid hook call" crash on every FastImage render, with logcat showing `Source: D:\interview-task\react-native-fast-image\dist\index.cjs.js` for the codegenNativeComponent deep-import warning - the library's dist/index.cjs.js lives OUTSIDE this app, so Metro resolved its `require('react')`/`require('react-native')` relative to the library's OWN node_modules (root package.json devDependencies: react/react-native), not this app's copies - two separate React instances loaded at once. `resolver.extraNodeModules` does NOT fix this (it is only a fallback for names that fail to resolve normally - react/react-native never fail to resolve, they just resolve to the wrong directory). Fixed via a custom `resolver.resolveRequest` that intercepts `react`/`react-native`/`react-native/*` and rewrites `context.originModulePath` to a path inside this app's own projectRoot before delegating back to `context.resolveRequest`, forcing Metro's directory-walk-up node_modules search to land on this app's copies regardless of which file (app or linked library) is doing the importing.
(4) `bun run android` (via `react-native.exe run-android`) does not work invoked through the Bash tool/Git-Bash on this machine: it spawns `gradlew.bat` in a way Git Bash's PATH breaks (`'gradlew.bat' is not recognized as an internal or external command`), and separately its interactive "Another process is running on port 8081, use 8082 instead?" prompt hangs forever with no stdin attached (CI=true did not suppress it). Worked around by using PowerShell directly: kill whatever is squatting on 8081 (`Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8081 -State Listen`), then `cd android && .\gradlew.bat installDebug` (PowerShell, not Bash), then separately start Metro (`bun run start`, Bash is fine for this one), `adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081`, `adb shell am start -n com.reactnativefastimageexample/.MainActivity`.
(5) Also found and killed several stray leftover background processes from earlier in the same session that were never cleaned up: a `jest --watch` left running from an early `bun run test -- -u` call that omitted CI=true, and a stale Metro instance squatting on port 8081 from an earlier ad-hoc `bun run start --port 8098` test that was supposedly killed but wasn't (wrong PID killed). These caused confusing symptoms (user saw the OLD pre-fix bundle being served) purely because of leftover process hygiene, not a real bug in the fix itself.
End state: confirmed via `adb shell screencap` - the app genuinely renders on Pixel_6 emulator (API 36/x86_64), FastImageView (Fabric) displaying images with border-radius clipping (circle + rounded-rect), GIF playback, priority-loading section, progress-callback section all visually correct. Some images in the priority section show as gray placeholders because Glide got HTTP 503 (no real internet egress from this sandboxed emulator) - a sandbox/network limitation, not an app bug.
why: Everything up to this point had only been verified via `gradlew assembleDebug` (a native-only build that never touches Metro/JS bundling at all), so this whole class of bugs (stale metro.config.js template, duplicate React instances, Windows/Git-Bash tooling friction) sat completely undetected through both migration phases. This is the actual end-to-end proof the New Architecture migration works, not just that native code compiles.
how_to_apply: Do not use the Bash tool to invoke `bun run android`/`react-native run-android` on this machine - always do the gradlew install step via PowerShell, and manage Metro/adb separately. Before troubleshooting a "module not found" or "Invalid hook call" from the example app again, check whether a STALE metro process is still running on 8081 first (`Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8081`) - many of the "still broken" reports during this session were actually just an old process serving a pre-fix bundle, not the fix failing. Do not touch metro.config.js's watchFolders/resolveRequest/unstable_enableSymlinks block without understanding both problems it solves (symlink following AND duplicate-React prevention) - removing either half reintroduces one of the two failure modes above.

summary: Full visual redesign of ReactNativeFastImageExample (light/dark theming, card-based example screens, restyled tab bar) - verified working end-to-end on the Android emulator in both themes
detail: User provided a mockup (light + dark side by side) and asked for a full app redesign, then simplified bottom tab labels to single words. Built: src/theme.ts (useTheme() hook wrapping useColorScheme(), auto light/dark, no manual toggle per user choice; FEATURE_COLORS palette, one accent per example section), src/IconAvatar.tsx (colored rounded-square/circle icon avatar, supports icon name or short text label for the GIF badge), src/ExampleCard.tsx (icon+title+subtitle card header wrapping each example - replaces the old Section+FeatureText bullet pattern entirely; supports a `featured` prop for the Priority card's accent border - approximated the mockup's gradient border with a solid accent color per user choice, no new native dependency). Deleted src/Section.tsx (fully superseded, zero remaining usages after migrating all 9 example screens to ExampleCard). Updated SectionFlex.tsx/FeatureText.tsx/Button.tsx/StatusBarUnderlay.tsx/ImageGrid.tsx to be theme-aware instead of hardcoded colors. Rewrote FastImageExamples.tsx header to match the mockup (icon avatar + title + subtitle + circular top-right button). Restyled index.tsx's bottom tab bar via @react-navigation/bottom-tabs's own tabBarActiveTintColor/tabBarStyle/tabBarLabelStyle options (no custom tabBar needed) and fixed a real pre-existing bug found along the way: the FastImage Example tab's icon name 'ios-information-circle' does not exist in the installed Ionicons glyph map (verified via node_modules/react-native-vector-icons/glyphmaps/Ionicons.json) - was rendering blank, swapped to 'home-outline'. Tab labels later simplified to single words via the `tabBarLabel` option (route `name` left unchanged): 'Home'/'Grid'/'Fast'. Also fixed ReactNativeFastImageExample/.eslintrc.js (extends: '@react-native-community' -> '@react-native' - another stale migration-era config reference that was blocking eslint entirely).
why: User wants the demo app to look like a modern, polished product rather than the bare-bones original template - senior UI/UX judgment applied: reused react-navigation's built-in tabBarActiveTintColor/tabBarStyle/tabBarLabelStyle APIs instead of hand-rolling a custom tab bar (confirmed available in the installed v6.6.1 by reading node_modules/@react-navigation/bottom-tabs/src/types.tsx directly, not assumed from memory), and avoided adding any new native dependency (e.g. for a true gradient border) given this repo's history of Windows CMake/native-dependency pain earlier in the same migration.
how_to_apply: Metro repeatedly served STALE bundles during this session despite file edits landing correctly on disk (confirmed via grep on live-fetched bundle output missing strings that were verified present in the source file). After any batch of rapid successive edits to many files, do not trust a single Metro instance left running from before the edits - kill it and restart with `bun run start --reset-cache`, then verify the new bundle actually contains an expected new string via curl+grep BEFORE reloading the app and concluding something is broken. All theme-driven colors live in src/theme.ts (Theme interface + FEATURE_COLORS) - add new example screens by importing ExampleCard + useTheme + a new FEATURE_COLORS entry, never hardcode colors again in this app.

summary: Ran security-review skill on the full migration+redesign diff, all 3 candidates scored 2/10 (excluded); user asked to fix them anyway - fixed 2, reverted the 3rd after it broke a real test and reintroduced a design flaw
detail: Findings from the review: (1) FastImageErrorEvent.java/FastImageRequestListener.java forwarded the raw Glide exception message to JS onError (Android only, iOS still sends empty payload) - fixed by removing the message field entirely, event now always carries an empty payload matching iOS parity. (2) src/index.tsx headers-array-reshape condition `(isFabricEnabled || Platform.OS === 'android')` uses a global (not platform-scoped) isFabricEnabled flag, so if iOS ever had Fabric enabled without this library's iOS Fabric support existing, headers would silently convert to array shape while ios/FastImage/RCTConvert+FFFastImage.m still expects NSDictionary. ATTEMPTED FIX: changed condition to `Platform.OS === 'android'` only - this broke `bun run test` immediately (iOS "renders" snapshot expects headers as array) and on reflection is WRONG: FastImageViewComponent (src/FastImageViewNativeComponent.ts) is the SAME shared Codegen spec used cross-platform, so once iOS Fabric support is eventually built (per docs/new-architecture-ios-followup.md), it will read the SAME array-shape headers as Android, not NSDictionary - the original `isFabricEnabled ||` condition is actually the forward-compatible correct design, not a bug. REVERTED this change back to original. (3) FastImageViewConverter.java's getHeaders() array branch called headersArray.getMap(i) without checking ReadableType.Map first, unlike the sibling Map-shape branch - fixed by adding the same `headersArray.getType(i) != ReadableType.Map` guard (skip malformed entries instead of throwing). No test/behavior regression from this one.
why: User explicitly asked to fix all 3 candidates one by one despite the security-review skill's own filtering excluding all of them (confidence 2/10 each, none crossed the >=8 report threshold) - reasonable defense-in-depth request. But finding (2)'s "fix" was actively wrong: always verify a security "fix" against the test suite and the actual forward-looking design intent before accepting it, especially when the finding was already flagged as low-confidence/dead-code by the review itself.
how_to_apply: If iOS Fabric support for this component is ever implemented (see docs/new-architecture-ios-followup.md), the new iOS Fabric component view MUST read headers as the array-of-{name,value} shape (matching src/FastImageViewNativeComponent.ts's NativeProps.headers type), not NSDictionary - do not "fix" the isFabricEnabled global-flag condition in src/index.tsx again without first building that iOS support, or the same test-breaking mistake will repeat.

summary: Fixed the Critical/High/Medium/Low findings from the senior-code-review pass (thread safety, duplicate ViewManager code, naming, fragile color math, unstable tabBarIcon components) - verified via real Gradle build + jest, added missed test coverage
detail:
Critical: FastImageOkHttpProgressGlideModule.java's DispatchingProgressListener.LISTENERS/PROGRESSES were plain HashMap/WeakHashMap mutated from OkHttp's background dispatcher thread (update()) AND the UI thread (expect()/forget()) with zero synchronization - swapped both to ConcurrentHashMap. While investigating this, found the SAME class of bug also applied to VIEWS_FOR_URLS (in FastImageViewManager, both oldarch/newarch) - not just the outer map but the INNER per-key List<FastImageViewWithUrl> too, since onProgress() (called from the OkHttp thread via the progress listener chain) iterates that list while onAfterUpdate/onDropViewInstance (UI thread) concurrently add/remove from it. Fixed both by creating a new shared android/src/main/java/com/dylanvann/fastimage/FastImageViewManagerHelpers.java: VIEWS_FOR_URLS is now ConcurrentHashMap<String, List<...>> with CopyOnWriteArrayList per key.
High: This same new helper class also fixed the "duplicate ViewManager code" finding - oldarch/newarch FastImageViewManager.java were ~90% identical (diffed directly), including THREE fully-duplicated private methods (isValidContextForGlide/getActivityFromContext/isActivityDestroyed) that had nothing to do with old/new-arch differences at all. Moved those + the VIEWS_FOR_URLS registry into the shared helper; both variant files now just delegate. Verified compiles for new-arch via a real `gradlew :react-native-fast-image:compileDebugJavaWithJavac` (BUILD SUCCESSFUL) - old-arch source set could NOT be build-verified since RN 0.82+ makes New Architecture mandatory and ignores `-PnewArchEnabled=false` (confirmed via the warning Gradle itself prints), so checked oldarch/FastImageViewManager.java by eye/grep for leftover references to removed symbols instead.
High: FastImageViewWithUrl.java line ~86 was STILL calling the old 3-arg `new FastImageErrorEvent(surfaceId, viewId, "Invalid source prop:" + mSource)` constructor that a PRIOR fix this session already removed from FastImageErrorEvent.java (down to 2-arg, no message field) - this file would not have compiled. Fixed the call site (drops the whole info-disclosure string entirely, matching the already-decided empty-payload approach) and this also resolved the compile error.
Medium: removed dead commented-out line in FastImageViewWithUrl.java (`//final GlideUrl glideUrl = ...`); fixed `glideUrl.toString()` -> `glideUrl.toStringUrl()` inconsistency in both FastImageViewManager.onDropViewInstance (was using a different method than every other call site in the codebase for the exact same map key - functionally likely equivalent today but inconsistent and a landmine if Glide's CacheKeyFactory is ever customized).
Medium: IconAvatar.tsx's `color + (theme.dark ? '33' : '18')` string concat assumed every color is a bare 6-digit hex - added an exported `withAlpha(color, alphaHex, fallback)` pure function that regex-validates hex format and falls back to `theme.placeholder` otherwise; added ReactNativeFastImageExample/src/IconAvatar.test.tsx (new test file - this repo's example app previously had ZERO component-level tests, only the App-test.tsx smoke test) covering valid hex, case-insensitivity, and every non-hex format (rgba, named colors, 3-digit/8-digit hex, empty string).
Low: hoisted the three tabBarIcon inline arrow functions in ReactNativeFastImageExample/src/index.tsx to module-scope named functions (renderHomeIcon/renderGridIcon/renderFastGridIcon) - this also cleared the pre-existing `react/no-unstable-nested-components` eslint warnings, confirmed via `eslint src` now returning zero output (previously 3 warnings).
Low: renamed generic single-letter/generic names - ResizeModeExample.tsx's `Col`/`p` -> `ResizeModeColumn`/`props`; LocalImagesExample.tsx's `Row`/`Image`(shadowed RN's own Image import)/`p` -> `LocalImageRow`/`LocalPreviewImage`/`props`.
Verification: root `bun run test` 21/21, example app `bun run test` 8/8 (new IconAvatar.test.tsx + existing App-test.tsx), `eslint src` zero output, and a REAL `gradlew assembleDebug` (not just compileDebugJavaWithJavac) - BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 301 tasks.
why: User asked to fix every finding from the code-review one by one without breaking the existing flow, and to add missed test coverage. Both real bugs (the compile error I found mid-fix, and the deeper VIEWS_FOR_URLS thread-safety bug beyond what the original review scoped) were only caught because every native change was verified against a REAL Gradle compile, not just visual inspection - this is a recurring lesson in this repo (see also `example-app-jest-and-dist-build-fixed` memory) about never trusting native/build changes without an actual build.
how_to_apply: FastImageViewManagerHelpers.java (android/src/main/java) is now the single source of truth for VIEWS_FOR_URLS bookkeeping and the isValidContextForGlide/getActivityFromContext/isActivityDestroyed trio - do not re-duplicate these into oldarch/newarch FastImageViewManager.java again; any future old/new-arch-shared logic should go there too. Old-architecture Android source set (android/src/oldarch) can no longer be build-verified on this RN version/toolchain (0.82+ forces New Architecture) - changes to it must be verified by careful manual symmetry-checking against the newarch variant (which CAN still be compiled), not by an actual build.
